newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Semicon up on fatter profit target.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Semicon up on fatter profit target.

text.p: Chip giant Taiwan Semiconductor surged at in early Monday trade after it said on Monday it would fatten its 1997 sales and profit targets by more than 20 percent within 10 days due to improving performance.
After 60 minutes at 0200 GMT, Taiwan Semicon had surged T$5.5 or 5.10 percent to T$113.5. Rival United Microelectronics was up T$2.5 or 2.36 percent to T$108.5.

"Because of expected sound recovery in the third quarter, other chipmakers, especially United Microelectronics, likely will follow Taiwan Semiconductor's plan to raise their 1997 profit and sales targets," said HSBC James Capel's Alex Chen.
A spokeswoman said Taiwan Semiconductor would unveil details of the revision in 10 days. Its current forecasts are for T$9.14 billion in net profits on sales of T$35.22 billion, she said.
"Due to improving performance and outlook, we have decided to raise our sales and profit targets for 1997 by more than 20 percent," a Taiwan Semiconductor spokeswoman told Reuters.
Independent electronics analyst Michael Hung forecast a reasonable market price for Taiwan Semiconductor of T$117 to T$165, and for United Microelectronics of T$82.8 to T$124.2.
In April, Taiwan Semiconductor announced it would launch a T$400 billion (US$14.3 billion), 10-year wafer fabrication project in the southern high-tech zone at Tainan.

Last week, United Microelectronics went its arch rival one better, announcing a mammoth T$500 billion (US$17.9 billion), 10-year wafer fab project that sharply upped the stakes in Taiwan's intense integrated circuit wars.

Both projects, once completed, would dwarf what until April was Taiwan's most ambitious investment project -- a US$9 billion petrochemical plant being built in central Taiwan by Formosa Plastics group.
